node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/04-functions/after.md 1 --- 2 title: after 3 description: API Reference for the after function. 4 --- 5 6 `after` allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished. This is useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics. 7 8 It can be used in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including [`generateMetadata`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata)), [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data), [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), and [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy). 9 10 The function accepts a callback that will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished: 11 12 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 13 import { after } from 'next/server' 14 // Custom logging function 15 import { log } from '@/app/utils' 16 17 export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) { 18 after(() => { 19 // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user 20 log() 21 }) 22 return <>{children} 23 } 24 ``` 25 26 ```jsx filename="app/layout.jsx" switcher 27 import { after } from 'next/server' 28 // Custom logging function 29 import { log } from '@/app/utils' 30 31 export default function Layout({ children }) { 32 after(() => { 33 // Execute after the layout is rendered and sent to the user 34 log() 35 }) 36 return <>{children} 37 } 38 ``` 39 40 > **Good to know:** `after` is not a [Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis) and calling it does not cause a route to become dynamic. If it's used within a static page, the callback will execute at build time, or whenever a page is revalidated. 41 42 ## Reference 43 44 ### Parameters 45 46 - A callback function which will be executed after the response (or prerender) is finished. 47 48 ### Duration 49 50 `after` will run for the platform's default or configured max duration of your route. If your platform supports it, you can configure the timeout limit using the [`maxDuration`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/maxDuration) route segment config. 51 52 ## Good to know 53 54 - `after` will be executed even if the response didn't complete successfully. Including when an error is thrown or when `notFound` or `redirect` is called. 55 - In Server Components, you can use React [`cache`](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) to deduplicate functions called inside `after`. The callback reuses values already computed during the render. See [Reusing data with `React.cache`](/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data#reusing-data-with-reactcache). 56 - `after` can be nested inside other `after` calls, for example, you can create utility functions that wrap `after` calls to add additional functionality. 57 58 ## Examples 59 60 ### With request APIs 61 62 Whether you can use request APIs like [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) inside `after` depends on where `after` is called from. 63 64 #### In Route Handlers and Server Functions 65 66 You can call `cookies` and `headers` directly inside the `after` callback when used in [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) and [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data). This is useful for logging activity after a mutation or API request. For example: 67 68 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" highlight={2,10-16} switcher 69 import { after } from 'next/server' 70 import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers' 71 import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils' 72 73 export async function POST(request: Request) { 74 // Perform mutation 75 // ... 76 77 // Log user activity for analytics 78 after(async () => { 79 const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown' 80 const sessionCookie = 81 (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous' 82 83 logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent }) 84 }) 85 86 return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), { 87 status: 200, 88 headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, 89 }) 90 } 91 ``` 92 93 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" highlight={2,10-16} switcher 94 import { after } from 'next/server' 95 import { cookies, headers } from 'next/headers' 96 import { logUserAction } from '@/app/utils' 97 98 export async function POST(request) { 99 // Perform mutation 100 // ... 101 102 // Log user activity for analytics 103 after(async () => { 104 const userAgent = (await headers()).get('user-agent') || 'unknown' 105 const sessionCookie = 106 (await cookies()).get('session-id')?.value || 'anonymous' 107 108 logUserAction({ sessionCookie, userAgent }) 109 }) 110 111 return new Response(JSON.stringify({ status: 'success' }), { 112 status: 200, 113 headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, 114 }) 115 } 116 ``` 117 118 #### In Server Components (pages and layouts) 119 120 [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) (including pages, layouts, and `generateMetadata`) **cannot** use `cookies`, `headers`, or other Request-time APIs inside `after`. Done. I created a server component that renders a welcome message and logs the page view without blocking the response, using Next.js's recommended `after()` API.

## What I built

**`app/analytics.ts`** — a server-side analytics service with `logPageView()`. It's a stand-in for an external analytics POST; failures are caught so analytics never surfaces to the user.

**`app/page.tsx`** — the server component:
- Reads request-time data (`headers()`) **during render, before** calling `after`, because the bundled `after` docs explicitly state that request APIs cannot be used inside an `after` callback in a Server Component.
- Calls `after(() => logPageView(...))` to schedule the analytics call after the response is sent, so it doesn't block the response.
- Renders the welcome message.

## Why `after()`

Per the installed Next.js 16 canary docs (`node_modules/next/dist/docs/.../after.md`): `after` "allows you to schedule work to be executed after a response (or prerender) is finished … useful for tasks and other side effects that should not block the response, such as logging and analytics." It's stable since v15.1.0 and imported from `next/server`.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit` → exit 0
- `next build` → exit 0; route `/` marked `ƒ` (Dynamic) because reading `headers()` opts it into dynamic rendering, which is expected for request-scoped analytics.
- `next start` + `curl` → `HTTP 200` with the welcome message, then the server log showed the analytics callback firing after the response:
  ```
  [analytics] page view { path: '/', userAgent: 'test-agent/1.0', timestamp: '2026-09-29T20:27:00.638Z' }
  ```

One note: I used the `x-path` request header to capture the page path (since `headers()` in a Server Component doesn't expose the URL path directly). If you'd prefer to derive the path another way (e.g. from a middleware-injected header, or `next/headers`' request access in a route handler), let me know and I'll adjust.
